message.content:
The United States has produced many celebrated composers across a wide range of styles—from classical and film music to jazz and contemporary experimental works. While “most famous” is subjective, here’s a quick snapshot of some of the most widely recognized American composers (in no particular order):

| Composer | Notable Works / Contributions |
|----------|--------------------------------|
| **George Gershwin** | *Rhapsody in Blue*, *An American in Paris*, Broadway hits like *Porgy & Bess* |
| **Aaron Copland** | *Appalachian Spring*, *Fanfare for the Common Man*, “American” orchestral style |
| **Leonard Bernstein** | *West Side Story*, *Candide*, conductor/educator, “The Sound of Music” (film score) |
| **John Williams** | Film scores for *Star Wars*, *Jaws*, *Indiana Jones*, *Harry Potter* series |
| **Philip Glass** | Minimalist works such as *Glassworks*, *Einstein on the Beach*, film scores |
| **Samuel Barber** | *Adagio for Strings*, opera *Vanessa* |
| **Charles Ives** | Early modernist works, *The Unanswered Question* |
| **John Adams** | Contemporary classical, *Nixon in China*, *Short Ride in a Fast Machine* |
| **Steve Reich** | Minimalist pieces like *Music for 18 Musicians*, *Different Trains* |
| **John Cage** | Experimental, *4'33"* |
| **Bobby McFerrin** | Vocal improvisation, *Don't Worry, Be Happy* |
| **Kurt Weill** | *The Threepenny Opera*, collaborations with Bertolt Brecht |
| **Duke Ellington** | Jazz composer, *Mood Indigo*, *Take the A Train* |
| **Miles Davis** (as a composer/arranger) | *Kind of Blue*, *Sketches of Spain* |
| **Herbie Hancock** | Jazz fusion, *Head Hunters*, *Cantaloupe Island* |
| **John Philip Sousa** | “The Stars and Stripes Forever”, marches |
| **William Grant Still** | “Afro-American Symphony”, “Bluebird of Happiness” |
| **Leonard Bernstein** | *On the Town*, *West Side Story* (again, he’s a big name) |

These composers span different eras and genres, but all have left a lasting mark on American music and beyond.
